newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KENDALL SET TO BECOME EVERTON MANAGER FOR THIRD TIME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KENDALL SET TO BECOME EVERTON MANAGER FOR THIRD TIME.

text.p: Howard Kendall is expected to be named as Everton manager for the third time on Thursday -- but his current club Sheffield United look set to sue Everton for 1.0 million pounds ($1.7 million) compensation.
Sheffield United chairman Mike McDonald said on Wednesday he wants the money in compensation from Everton for Kendall who was appointed Sheffield United manager 18 months ago.
"I feel I have been kicked in the teeth," he said.

United player Mitch Ward said: "This has come as a total shock to most of the players and I am very disappointed. All you can do is pick yourself up and get on with it, but it is a big disappointment."
Kendall, who took United into the first division play-off final last season, was not Everton's first choice for the job.

Originally he was linked with the move in tandem with Andy Gray, a former Everton player, who looked set to become manager before deciding to remain with Sky Television where he works as a commentator and analyst.
Kendall however is expected to commence his third spell in charge of Everton on Thursday.

McDonald said: "I brought him back into football when no-one would apparently give him a job. Now he has let me down. Basically he told me then what he told the papers that I would have to kick him out of Bramall Lane to be rid of him."

McDonald, who is now in negotiations over compensation for Kendall with Everton counterpart Peter Johnson, added: "Everton value Howard Kendall enough to hand him control of their club. How do you put a figure on experience know-how and a success rate?"

The United chairman is hoping that there will be a replacement for Kendall at Bramall Lane before the players report back for training on July 9, with former Everton boss Joe Royle rumoured to be interested.
Kendall returned to Manchester airport on Wednesday confirming he would be returning to Everton, subject to further negotiations.
"I'm forever grateful to Mike McDonald and the people at Sheffield United because they gave me the opportunity to come back into football. Hopefully they will regard that as a job nearly done.
"In terms of Everton, they are very special. I'm looking forward to it and I thank sheffield United for understanding that."
Speaking on BBC Radio he added: "I spent 17 years as a player and twice as manager at Everton and it holds something special for me. I'm delighted and honoured to go back there."

Kendall, is the most successful manager in Everton's history, winning two league titles and the European Cup Winners' Cup and, despite an ill-fated first return to Goodison, fans would welcome him taking over again.
He has also managed Blackburn, Athletic Bilbao, Manchester City, Greek club Xanthi and Notts County.
His first target at Everton will be England midfield ace Paul Ince, with Johnson said to have guaranteed Kendall 20.0 million pounds ($33 million) to rebuild the squad at Goodison.
